title: Aldercroft Software — H1 trading update
note: Held out from any parameter fitting. Used once, to check whether the calibration established on the hero note transfers to a stimulus it has never seen. Deliberately a different sector, a different document type, and a different balance of good and bad news, so transfer is a real test rather than a rehearsal. Whether it holds is reported either way.
texts: Aldercroft Software reported first-half recurring revenue of $312m, up 11%.
Net revenue retention fell to 104% from 118%.
Gross new customer additions were 214, against 340 in the comparable period.
Churn was concentrated in the small business tier.
Management is repositioning toward enterprise accounts.
Enterprise now represents 58% of recurring revenue.
Average contract length extended from 18 months to 31 months.
Deferred revenue rose 22% to $198m.
Sales and marketing spend fell from 41% to 34% of revenue.
The company reported its first positive operating income of $9m.
Free cash flow was $41m, ahead of operating income owing to the deferred revenue build.
Share-based compensation of $58m is excluded from adjusted figures.
Diluted share count increased 6% year on year.
The company holds $420m of cash and has no drawn debt.
A $150m convertible note matures in September 2027.
The conversion price sits 40% above the current share price.
Two of the four named executive officers joined within the past nine months.
The company disclosed a security incident affecting a single-tenant deployment, since remediated.
No customer data was exfiltrated, according to a third-party forensic review.
Full-year guidance was narrowed to 9 to 11% recurring revenue growth, from 9 to 13%.
